newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--payroll wariness limits rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--payroll wariness limits rise.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds gained around an eighth of a point at the long end as traders' hopes that the economy can keep growing without setting off inflation were strengthened by the latest economic data.
"The market is up a little bit, probably quoted up an 0.01 basis point," a trader said, referring to the long end.
Nor were the gains confined to this end of the yield curve, as a trader of short-term municipals said: "It's very firm, up a couple of basis points," noting there were few available supplies.

Despite predictions from the New York City mayor and comptroller that New York City would capture a record $700 million to $800 million budget surplus when its fiscal 1997 year ends on June 30, traders said the city's debt showed no immediate response.

"They have been trading increasingly better compared to the rest of the market...but is there an extra pop because of the news story? No," said a trader, explaining that New York City's debt has outpaced the overall market for the past six to nine months due to widespread views that the city's finances were improving. Other traders have said the gains began around 18 months ago.

For the overall market, a cap to this week's over one-point rally was expected to start setting in shortly as traders were expected to square positions ahead of the release on Friday morning of the capstone of this week's economic reports, the crucial payrolls data for April.
"The number this morning was fairly decent for the market but I think the upside is a little limited with tomorrow's number staring you in the face," a trader said.
He was referring to the National Association of Purchasing Management report, which is a broad gauge of manufacturning strength or weakness.

The Association said that its lead index fell to 54.2 from 55.0 in March. The number was above forecasts for a 53.6 reading in April, but economists said the prices index, which fell to 49.6 from 50.9 in March, should put U.S. credit markets in a buoyant mood.

However, the payrolls data for April could rock the market out of its recent rally if it shows the economy is growing at a fast clip, sparking fears that inflation might be heating up. The report is expected to find employers added 211,000 jobs, while the unemployment rate steadied at 5.2 percent, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists.
In the muni secondary, bids on Chicago, Illinois, Board of Education Chicago School Reform of 2020 were four basis points lower at 5.93 percent. They have a coupon of 5-3/4 percent.
And Denver, Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of 2025, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid two basis points lower at 5.87 percent.
In debt futures, June municipal futures gained eight ticks to 109-17/32, while June Treasury bonds firmed five ticks to 114-19/32. The MOB spread eased to 158 ticks.
